author: Vox
description:
It’s clear that the youngest generation of voters isn’t the same as the ones that came before. So, what’s up with the kids? 

Gen Z researcher Rachel Janfaza joins Vox’s Astead Herndon to discuss how young voters are prioritizing economic survival, confronting their anxieties related to AI-job displacement, and searching for pragmatic, transparent leaders who address their everyday challenges.

00:00 Astead’s love-hate relationship with Gen Z
05:04 The theory of two Gen Z’s
06:19 How the pandemic broke Gen Z
09:48 Growing up with a phone in one hand
16:15 Rejection of the algorithm
17:56 The drivers of economic anxiety
22:08 AI and the future of work
25:25 The gender divide, explained
31:43 Hope for a post-Trump politics
32:51 Takeaways

Gen Z researcher Rachel Janfaza says that young women have bonded politically in response to major social and cultural events of the past decade. Gen Z men, she says, don’t have similar spaces.
